transcript.text: Thank you all for joining this litigation-planning meeting. As you know, we're dealing with a former employee's trade secrets lawsuit that seeks broad inspection of our devices and systems. The case-management conference is next month and no discovery has been exchanged yet. Our priorities are clear: protect the company's confidential information and keep defense costs controlled. Before I approve the initial defense plan, I need discovery counsel and insurance-coverage counsel to identify any facts that should shape our approach. Let's start with discovery counsel -- what do we need to know to build our protective strategy?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to share a critical fact that should shape our entire defense strategy. My forensic review of the former employee's company laptop has confirmed that exactly three identified trade-secret files were copied to the device. Importantly, the review found no customer data on the device and no evidence of any additional copying beyond those three files. This significantly narrows the scope of what's actually at issue. My report is still awaiting final partner review and hasn't been added to the case plan yet, but this finding should drive our approach to the protective order and help us push back against the broad inspection demands in the complaint.

transcript.text: Elena, I need to share an important coverage fact that will directly shape our defense plan. I've reviewed the applicable policy endorsement, and the trade-secret defense is covered subject to a $75,000 self-insured retention, insurer-approved panel counsel, and a requirement that we obtain written insurer consent before engaging any forensic vendor. The endorsement is currently in the risk department's file and has not been attached to this matter yet. This means we need to factor the SIR into our cost projections, ensure our counsel selections align with the insurer's panel, and critically, we should not move forward with any forensic vendor engagement without first securing written insurer consent. I'll work on getting the endorsement formally attached to the matter and coordinating with the insurer, but these constraints need to be built into the initial defense plan now.
